newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian reinsurers become global players - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Australian reinsurers become global players - S&P.

text.p: Australia's reinsurance market is evolving into a globally-recognised centre with new entrants and a large capital market, Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday.
"Australia geographically is well placed to underwrite reinsurance business in the Asian market," Michael Vine, S&P's associate director for insurance said in S&P's monthly CreditFocus publication.
"Australian insurance entities are developing strong relationships in the region and possess the underwriting expertise necessary for assessing natural disaster risks," Vine said.
"As the world's third-largest buyer of catastrophic reinsurance, the Australian and New Zealand reinsurance markets are reqarded as important from a global perspective," Vine said.
"These markets will help to balance the spread of risk for major global players, away from a concentration in Europe or the U.S.," he added.

He said the willingness of shareholders to support pure reinsurance and catastrophe risk companies had led to the recent establishment of two stand-alone listed reinsurers, Reinsurance Australia Corp Ltd, and New Cap Reinsurance Corp Ltd.
S&P said emergence of companies such as these was part of a worldwide trend of allocating capital resources to reinsurance activities under defined legal and ownership structures.

"While the local market shares the current worldwide conditions of softening premium rates with strong competition, ample capacity, and ongoing profitability, the eventual bottom of the underwriting cycle in Australia is not expected to be as severe as in past years, given the greater market stability and thirst for profitability and shareholder return," Vine said.
